title: An improved lower-bound conjecture for the tripartite nullity
statement:
Let $V_1,V_2,V_3$ be the local qudit vector spaces with dimensions $d_1,d_2,d_3$, and let $n_a$ be the corresponding one-party nullities. For a tripartite state $v\in V_1\otimes V_2\otimes V_3$, let $n_{1,2,3}$ denote the nullity of the common kernel space $K_{1,2,3}(v)$. **The improved tripartite-nullity lower-bound conjecture.** The nullity $n_{1,2,3}$ satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
n_{1,2,3}&\ge n_{1}\bigl((d_{2}-n_{2})(d_{3}-n_{3})-(d_{1}-n_{1})\bigr)+n_{2}\bigl((d_{1}-n_{1})(d_{3}-n_{3})-(d_{2}-n_{2})\bigr)\\
&\quad+n_{3}\bigl((d_{1}-n_{1})(d_{2}-n_{2})-(d_{3}-n_{3})\bigr)\\
&\quad+\max\bigl\{n_{1}(d_{2}n_{3}+n_{2}d_{3}-n_{2}n_{3}),n_{2}(d_{1}n_{3}+n_{1}d_{3}-n_{1}n_{3}),n_{3}(d_{1}n_{2}+n_{1}d_{2}-n_{1}n_{2})\bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is presented as a stronger empirically supported lower bound for the tripartite nullity and hence for the analysis of tripartite entanglement classes. Its validity remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10728

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).
source_name: Roman V. Buniy and Thomas W. Kephart, “Tripartite entanglement of qudits”, arXiv:2412.10728 (2024).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A 2024 paper left the stronger bound open, while a posted argument claims a complete proof that has not been independently verified.
progress.summary:
Buniy and Kephart proposed the improved lower bound in 2024 for the common nullity of a tripartite tensor, strengthening earlier bounds. The paper records it as Conjecture 3.4 and leaves its validity unresolved.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10728)*

**Known results**

- Buniy and Kephart (2024) report extensive empirical evidence for the lower-bound conjectures.
- The allowed values of the three one-party nullities are characterized completely, but only lower and upper bounds are known for $n_{1,2,3}$.


**Posted attempt**

A reader-written argument claims a complete proof: after decomposing into active and null sectors, it derives an identity reducing the conjectured inequality to $\kappa(v)+\min\{a,b,c\}\geq 0$. This attempt has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture has empirical support and a posted unverified proof attempt, but no independently verified proof or counterexample is recorded.

*Caveats. The claimed derivation is unreviewed, so the conjecture cannot yet be classified as resolved.*

solutions.body:
Let \(v\in V_1\otimes V_2\otimes V_3\), let \(d_i=\dim V_i\), let \(n_i=\dim K_i(v)\), and set \(r_i=d_i-n_i\). Thus \(r_i\) is the rank of the \(i\)-th flattening of \(v\). Choose a basis in each factor and its corresponding dual basis so that \(v\) is supported on
\[
R_1\otimes R_2\otimes R_3,\qquad \dim R_i=r_i,
\]
with complementary null-coordinate spaces \(N_i\) of dimensions \(n_i\). Let \(\kappa(v)\geq0\) be the common-kernel dimension of the three pair-contraction maps restricted to the active spaces.

Splitting the tensor in the common-kernel equations according to the eight coordinate sectors of
\[
(R_1\oplus N_1)\otimes(R_2\oplus N_2)\otimes(R_3\oplus N_3)
\]
gives the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_{1,2,3}(v)
={}&\kappa(v)
+n_1(r_2r_3-r_1)+n_2(r_1r_3-r_2)+n_3(r_1r_2-r_3)\\
&+n_1n_2r_3+n_1r_2n_3+r_1n_2n_3+n_1n_2n_3. \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]

Indeed, the all-active sector contributes \(\kappa(v)\). In the sector \(N_1\otimes R_2\otimes R_3\), the contractions involving the first factor vanish automatically, while the remaining contraction has rank \(r_1\) on \(R_2\otimes R_3\), independently for each of the \(n_1\) null coordinates. This sector therefore contributes \(n_1(r_2r_3-r_1)\); the other one-null sectors follow by symmetry. Every sector containing at least two null factors is annihilated by all three pair contractions, giving the four remaining terms. Different support sectors have disjoint active/null output blocks, so these contributions form a direct sum.

Set
\[
L=\sum_{\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}}n_i(r_jr_k-r_i),\quad
a=r_1n_2n_3,\quad b=n_1r_2n_3,\quad c=n_1n_2r_3,\quad
\tau=n_1n_2n_3.
\]
Then (1) becomes
\[
n_{1,2,3}(v)=\kappa(v)+L+a+b+c+\tau. \tag{2}
\]

The three expressions inside the maximum in the conjectured bound are respectively
\[
b+c+\tau,\qquad a+c+\tau,\qquad a+b+\tau.
\]
Therefore their maximum equals
\[
a+b+c+\tau-\min\{a,b,c\}.
\]
Subtracting the proposed lower bound from (2) leaves exactly
\[
\kappa(v)+\min\{a,b,c\}\geq0.
\]
Hence the conjectured inequality holds for every tripartite tensor.
